key_insight: Adding 1 wt.% CeO₂ or La₂O₃ to HVOF-sprayed WC–12Co reduced porosity, refined grains, and increased microhardness by 6% and 4%, respectively.
engineering_relevance: Rare-earth oxide reinforcement offers a route to harder, more wear-resistant WC–12Co coatings without compromising bond strength under the tested conditions.
method: Deposit unreinforced and CeO₂- or La₂O₃-reinforced WC–12Co coatings using HVOF.
Compare microstructure, phase composition, microhardness, and adhesive bond strength.
Evaluate abrasive wear and friction; examine worn surfaces using SEM.
evidence_signal: WC–12Co–1La₂O₃ achieved the minimum wear rate of 3.5 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), while WC–12Co–1CeO₂ showed the lowest friction coefficient of 0.4; unreinforced bond strength was 73.60 ± 5 MPa.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or wear and friction variability, limiting extrapolation to service environments.
paper_title: EFFECT OF CEO2 AND LA2O3 REINFORCEMENTS ON MECHANICAL, TRIBOLOGICAL AND MICROSTRUCTURAL PROPERTIES OF WC–12CO COATING BY HIGH-VELOCITY OXYGEN FUEL DEPOSITION TECHNIQUE
